cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: The Conspiracy Expands
cards.instruction: Use every denial, coincidence, and missing detail as proof that more people and higher stakes are involved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The toaster receipt's gone. The shop has someone inside this house. Don't touch the recycling until I've checked it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I probably put it in there. We can get a replacement receipt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Never replace evidence before examining it. The shop prints a new version while the collectors remove the original. Convenient.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Every shop prints replacements. I'll ask the high-street traders' group.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You'd alert their coordinating body. Please let me handle the enquiries before the whole high street knows we're onto them.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 controls the recycling, A3 corrects replacement handling and A5 blocks group contact, making expert investigation enlarge the conspiracy.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 disposal and copy solution become A3 coordinated destruction; B4 traders' group becomes A5 coordination centre.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers a useful remedy; B4 tries a plausible local contact, although why a group rather than shop is not yet made explicit.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 named group as the larger organization and changes who may make enquiries.

specificity.evidence: A1 toaster receipt missing and B2 replacement establish the practical problem beneath false suspicions.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 evidence correction and A5 contact prevention are direct acts; the short Convenient adds distrust rather than a new theory.
